content.text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with four substituents:

- NO2 on the top-left carbon
- NH2 on the carbon to its right (top-right of the ring)
- Br on the bottom-right carbon
- a methyl group, drawn as a bare line, on the bottom-left carbon

The NH2 carbon sits between the NO2 carbon and the Br carbon, so the nitro and bromo groups are both ortho to the amine. The methyl group is para to the amine.

This is 2-bromo-4-methyl-6-nitroaniline.

Writing the SMILES from the NH2 carbon: Nc1c(Br)cc(C)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]

Checking the ring: c1 (NH2) – c(Br) – c(H) – c(CH3) – c(H) – c1(NO2). This gives six ring atoms, and the substituent positions match the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1cc(Br)c(N)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1
